questions.prompt: Match each life process to its meaning.

pairs.right: Getting rid of waste made in the body

questions.explain: MRS GREN: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition.
Only living things show all seven life processes.

questions.prompt: A car moves, uses oxygen to burn fuel and gives out waste gases. Why is it NOT alive?
options: It cannot grow, reproduce or sense its surroundings by itself
questions.explain: Living things must show ALL the life processes.

questions.prompt: A mimosa (touch-me-not) plant folds its leaves when touched. Which life process does this show?
A dry seed shows no signs of life for months, then sprouts when watered. What is the best conclusion?
options: It was dead and came back to life
questions.explain: Seeds respire very slowly while dormant.

questions.prompt: A salt crystal in a jar gets bigger every day. Adam says, “It’s growing, so it must be alive!” Use evidence to argue for or against his claim.
questions.modelAnswer: Adam is wrong. The crystal grows only by particles of salt adding to its outside, not by taking in food and using it. It does not respire, sense its surroundings, excrete, reproduce or take in nutrition. Living things must show all seven life processes, so one process (growth) is not enough evidence that something is alive.
rubric: States the crystal is not alive
Explains how crystal growth differs from living growth
Refers to the other life processes it lacks
questions.explain: Criterion C: evaluate a claim using evidence.
